title: Register each feature in exactly one wagon manifest

facts.note: Wagon manifests (wagon_manifest = the wagon's _features.yaml) are identifiable by file name; no particular plan directory layout is assumed.
Feature definitions and wagon manifests touched, read or assessed by the planner, wherever they live in the repository.
Any operation on a feature or wagon manifest, including content-only edits and read/assessment; the invariant holds for every feature at all times, with no content-based exclusion.
Needs a repository-wide observer that extracts every feature id and cross-references all wagon _features.yaml entries, so pre-existing orphans or duplicates surface even without a lifecycle change.
Planning task mentions features, wagons or manifests.

fires: Planner adds a new feature but does not list it in any wagon's _features.yaml.
Planner moves a feature to another wagon and lists it in both the old and new wagon manifests.
Planner edits a wagon's _features.yaml to add or remove a feature entry.
Planner reviews or plans work on an existing feature and discovers it is listed in no wagon manifest, or in more than one, even though nothing about it is being changed.

Planner edits only the acceptance or WMBT content of a feature: the rule applies; if the feature is already listed in exactly one wagon manifest it is compliant and no registration change is needed, otherwise the registration must be repaired.
doesNotFire: Changes that touch neither features nor wagon manifests and whose task does not concern features, wagons or manifests (e.g. pure implementation code with no plan artifacts).

given: A feature exists in the plan, and wagon manifests (each wagon's _features.yaml listing its features) record which wagon owns which feature.
when: You create, change (including acceptance/WMBT-only edits), move, remove or assess any feature, or edit a wagon manifest. A feature already listed in exactly one manifest is compliant and needs no registration change.
then: Register each feature under exactly one wagon's _features.yaml manifest.
prefer: Add the feature's entry to its owning wagon's _features.yaml in the same change that creates the feature, following the entry format already used in that manifest.
When moving a feature between wagons, remove the entry from the old wagon's manifest and add it to the new one in the same change.
Where the repository places features under their wagon's directory, list the feature in that wagon's manifest so ownership and location agree.
avoid: Orphan features that no wagon manifest lists.
Listing the same feature in two or more wagons' _features.yaml manifests.
Leaving stale manifest entries that point to removed or renamed features.
why: A feature belongs to exactly one wagon; the wagon manifest is the link that makes that ownership explicit and traceable.
evidence: Every feature id appears in exactly one wagon's _features.yaml; none appear in zero or several.
Proposed verification approach (not a source requirement): a reviewer checks the diff to confirm that new or moved features have matching manifest entries added and old ones removed.
verifier_detail: Term wagon_manifest: the wagon's _features.yaml that lists its features.

Metadata: disposition documentation-only, severity 2. Parity records implementation_preserved=false (no detector implementation was carried over). The source does not say how compliance is established, and defines no manifest entry schema or path-to-wagon mapping; use the entry format already present in the repository's manifests.

additions.text: Preferences for registering in the same change using the existing manifest entry format, handling moves, and aligning manifest ownership with on-disk location where the repository places features under wagon directories.
additions.justification: Concrete moves derived from the single statement and the graph edges (requires planner.wagon.features; runs_alongside atdd-bun.topology.plan-location). They add no obligation beyond 'exactly one wagon'; the location preference is conditional because the source defines no path-to-wagon mapping.

additions.text: Orphan, duplicate and stale manifest entries.
additions.justification: Direct negations of 'exactly one', plus the stale-entry consequence of moves and removals.

The source has no activation section. Activation is derived from the statement's subject (each feature, _features.yaml) and kept unconditional: acceptance/WMBT-only edits are an applicable, already-compliant case, not an exclusion.

additions.justification: The source states an unconditional invariant. The 'when' covers every engagement with a feature, so it does not narrow the rule.
